metadata.title: Security Assessment Results - Trusted Cloud (Microsoft 365)
metadata.remarks: Trusted-Cloud assessment for Microsoft 365 with tenant data hosted in Canada. Identifies contextual data sovereignty risk due to U.S. jurisdiction in light of emerging Canadian digital sovereignty policy (2025–2026).

findings.title: Foreign Jurisdiction over Canada-Hosted Productivity Data
findings.description: The Microsoft 365 tenant is geographically pinned to Canada, with Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Teams data hosted in Canadian data centres. However, Microsoft is a U.S.-owned provider and remains subject to U.S. jurisdiction. Emerging Canadian digital sovereignty policy (2025–2026) emphasizes jurisdictional autonomy over sensitive data beyond physical residency, introducing forward-looking governance and procurement considerations for certain data classes and regulated contexts.

associated-risk.title: Contextual Sovereignty Risk for User Content
associated-risk.description: While residency requirements are satisfied, foreign legal jurisdiction over provider operations may become misaligned with future Canadian federal procurement rules, critical-infrastructure requirements, or sector-specific restrictions for protected or sensitive data.

remediations.title: Manage Data Sovereignty through Classification and Policy Controls
remediations.description: Address jurisdictional sovereignty risk through governance and contextual use controls rather than technical remediation of the Microsoft 365 platform.

tasks.title: Apply Data Classification and Use Scoping
tasks.description: Define permitted Microsoft 365 use by data classification (e.g., Institutional, Protected B, Protected C) in alignment with evolving Canadian sovereignty requirements.

tasks.title: Maintain Privacy Impact Assessments
tasks.description: Conduct and update Privacy Impact Assessments documenting Canadian residency, U.S. jurisdiction exposure, and compensating controls.

tasks.title: Monitor Sovereignty Policy and Platform Options
tasks.description: Track changes to Canadian digital sovereignty policy and evaluate sovereign or hybrid collaboration alternatives for restricted contexts.
